title: policy-jigsaws-templating-and-siem-field-contracts
body:
Purpose and intent:

This is a working note (policy jigsaw) collecting small, re-usable IAM policy templates, role-tenancy crosswalks, and the SIEM field contract we want to land for automated evidence exports. The goal is a lightweight set of building blocks engineers and SREs can compose for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments without having to rewrite logging or evidence wiring for every change.

Scope:
- IAM role naming conventions and a compact role matrix for each hosting mode (hosted / dedicated / private).
- A few policy templates (least-privilege first) for common operations: model-deploy, inference-agent, telemetry-ingest, billing-read.
- Evidence payload field mapping to SIEM ingestion (document the minimum fields every evidence artifact must include).
- Operational patterns for Just-in-Time (JIT) elevation, temporary role TTL, and audit evidence retention triggers.

High-level principles (short):
- Principle: minimal scope per role, composed via policy fragments ("jigsaws") so we can reuse standard fragments across environments.
- Principle: evidence must be machine-readable, contain stable identifiers (tenant_id, deployment_id, request_id), and include provenance (actor, auth_method, token_lifetime).
- Principle: keep hosted exports opinionated; allow customers of Dedicated/Private to opt into our SIEM contract or map to their own sink (provide mapping helpers).

Role matrix (compact):
Columns: role_id | purpose | allowed-environments | elevation-allowed | evidence-tier
- infra-service-model-deployer | model lifecycle (upload/publish/rollback) | hosted,dedicated | no (requires approval flow) | high
- infra-runtime-agent | manage inference runner (start/stop,scale) | dedicated,private | yes (JIT, 1h TTL) | high
- telemetry-sink-writer | write-only to SIEM/observability pipeline | hosted,dedicated,private | no | medium
- billing-reader | read billing/export usage | hosted,dedicated | no | low
- tenant-admin | tenant-level config, keys, secrets | hosted,dedicated,private | limited (timebound elevation allowed) | high

Notes about naming: role IDs should be "svc-<domain>-<capability>" for service roles and "user-<team>-<capability>" for human roles. Keep length <= 64 chars. Avoid embedding environment names in role IDs; environment scope is stored in the role binding metadata.

Policy fragments (jigsaw pieces) - patterns and examples (use as templates, replace placeholders):

1) Read-only secret accessor fragment (minimal):
- description: grant read to KMS/secret-store for a specific key prefix
- statement (pseudo):
  - effect: allow
    actions: [secrets:Get, secrets:List]
    resources: [arn:secret:${tenant_id}:${secret_prefix}*]
    conditions: [request:source_environment == ${environment}]

2) Inference-runner control fragment (scale & health ops):
- description: start/stop and scale routes for serving nodes
- allowed actions: instance:Start, instance:Stop, instance:AdjustCapacity
- guard: only from infra-service principal or via approved runbook

3) SIEM write fragment (narrow):
- description: ability to push audit records to the evidence-queue
- allowed actions: events:PushToQueue
- resources: evidence-queue:${env_region}:${tenant_bucket}

Policy assembly notes:
- Compose fragments into environment-scoped policies. Example: for a dedicated runtime agent, assemble [inference-runner-control] + [kms-read-shortlived] + [siem-write] with explicit condition on binding.signed_by == "infra-signer".
- Keep policy size small; where cloud provider limits policy size, prefer referencing managed-policy fragments.

Environment-specific rules (short):
- Hosted: default to platform-managed keys, SIEM endpoint is Redwood-central (we push both raw events and summarized evidence). Customer tenant_admin cannot access infra-service roles. Any elevation requires manual approval through Recharge flow (Confluence link in artifacts).
- Dedicated: customer-owned VPCs and optional KMS. By default we allow telemetry-sink-writer to target Redwood observability but provide a toggle. Runtime agent roles may be bound to customer-managed identity providers; evidence exports must include mapping to the Redwood tenant_id for cross-correlation.
- Private/on-prem: no outbound push to Redwood SIEM by default. Provide an adapter shim that transforms Redwood evidence contract into customer SIEM format. For onboarding, include a mapping table and an example script in GitHub.

Evidence record minimal contract (flattened) - every event we export must include these fields (as top-level fields on the event JSON):
- event_ts (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_type (e.g., iam:role_bind, deployment:publish, inference:request)
- tenant_id (stable UUID)
- actor_id (user or service principal id)
- actor_type (user|service|external)
- role_id (the role that was used or escalated to)
- request_id (correlation id)
- resource (path or ARN-like identifier)
- decision (allow|deny|escalate|fallback)
- evidence_level (low|medium|high)
- policy_version (policy or fragment tag)
- ttl_seconds (if temporary credential)
- provenance_token_hash (short hash of auth token for attribution)

SIEM field mapping notes:
- Map event_ts -> @timestamp in the SIEM index. Map tenant_id -> tenant.id, actor_id -> user.id, role_id -> iam.role.id, request_id -> trace.id.
- Keep a flat top-level schema to avoid expensive nested parsing in ingestion pipelines. Attach freeform 'meta' field for non-critical extras (max size 2KB).
- When exporting to external SIEMs (customer-managed), provide both the flattened event and an optional compressed payload under payload.bz64 for full forensic context.

Automated evidence export flow (sketch):
1) Event generated (platform or customer runtime).
2) Local collector enriches record (adds tenant_id, request_id, policy_version).
3) Collector pushes into evidence-queue with evidence-level tag.
4) Export worker pulls, validates contract fields, signs with export key, and forwards to SIEM sink (internal or customer).
5) Export worker stores a replica in cold-evidence-store for compliance (retention per SLA).

Operational patterns - JIT elevation and TTL:
- For runtime operators that need temporary elevated roles, use a JIT proxy that issues short-lived credentials with a default TTL of 1 hour. JIT requests must include: reason, approver_id (if manual), and a dataset of related ticket/PR id.
- TTL heuristics: default 1h for infra ops; 15m for sensitive key material access; max 24h only with explicit justification.
- Evidence to capture for JIT: original_role, elevated_role, requested_at, granted_at, expiry_at, approver_id, approval_token_id.

Examples and quick templates (copy-paste friendly):
- Example SIEM flat event (pseudo-JSON, single-line for ingestion):
  {"event_ts":"2026-02-18T17:12:03Z","event_type":"iam:role_bind","tenant_id":"t-8f9a2b","actor_id":"svc-infra-xyz","actor_type":"service","role_id":"svc-infra-runtime","request_id":"r-4c5d6e","resource":"/deployments/d-12345","decision":"allow","evidence_level":"high","policy_version":"p-v12","ttl_seconds":"3600","provenance_token_hash":"h:7b2f"}

- Minimal policy fragment example (pseudo-DSL):
  fragment kms-read-shortlived {
    allow: [secrets:Get, secrets:List]
    resource: arn:secrets:${tenant_id}:${prefix}*
    condition: request.source_environment == ${environment}
  }

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Q: Do we require signed export for all hosted evidence? (tradeoff: security vs. processing latency)
- Q: For dedicated customers that opt-in to Redwood SIEM, do we normalize tenant_ids across different identity providers or require the customer to provide mapping?
- TODO: Add example mappings for Splunk HEC and Elastic Ingest pipelines (story created: JIRA-SEC-1031).
- TODO: Draft a minimal onboarding checklist for private deployments that includes evidence adapter deployment and field validation tests.

References / pointers:
- Confluence: SEC Evidence Export design (CONFLUENCE-SEC-2452)
- Jira: role-naming-canonicalization (JIRA-SEC-998)
- GitHub: iam-templates repo, folder /fragments

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally mixes high-level policy with runnable fragments to accelerate adoption. Please comment inline if a fragment is too prescriptive for your environment.
- If you have an existing policy fragment we should absorb, paste it here and tag me (Asha) in Slack for quick merge.

Last edited by Asha Menon on 2026-02-20.
